title: Type 2 diabetes, three-month follow-up
notice: Synthetic conversation written for a software demo. Every name, date, phone number and address is invented. Not medical advice.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Hi, Mr. Mitchell, I'm Doctor Raman. Good to see you again. Before we start, can you confirm your date of birth for me?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: July 19th, 1967.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Thank you. And we have your address as 1187 Birchwood Drive, Mississauga, L5G 2K9. Is that still current?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Still the same, yes.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: And your phone number, 905-555-0147?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's the house phone. My wife, Linda, usually answers it.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: That's fine. So this is your three-month diabetes check. How have things been going?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Honestly, not great. The holidays were rough. I've been eating a lot more bread and sweets than I should.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: That's common. Are you still taking the metformin, 1000 milligrams twice a day?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Mostly. I skip the evening dose sometimes because it upsets my stomach. Maybe three or four times a week I miss it.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: What kind of stomach upset?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Cramping and loose stools, usually an hour or so after I take it.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Okay. What have your sugars been like at home?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: In the mornings they're usually between 8 and 10.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: And exercise?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I walk the dog maybe twice a week. Less since it got cold.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Any chest pain, shortness of breath, or problems with your vision?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No chest pain. My eyes seem fine, but I haven't had an eye exam in about two years. The one thing is my feet. Sometimes at night I get tingling in my toes.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Both feet?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, both.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Okay. Are you taking any supplements?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My brother-in-law keeps telling me to try cinnamon pills, but I haven't started them.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: I'd hold off on those. There isn't good evidence that they help. Now, your A1c from last week came back at 8.1 percent. In the spring it was 7.4.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: So it's going up.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: It is. Your blood pressure today is 142 over 88, and your weight is 98 kilograms, up two from last time. On the foot exam, your pulses are good, but sensation with the monofilament is reduced at both big toes. That fits with early nerve changes from diabetes.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's worrying.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: It's a sign we should tighten things up. Here's what I'd suggest. First, let's switch your metformin to the extended-release form, still 1000 milligrams twice a day. It's usually easier on the stomach. Second, I'd like to add a medication called empagliflozin, 10 milligrams once a day. It lowers sugar and also protects the heart and kidneys.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Any side effects?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: It can cause genital yeast infections and make you pee more, so drink enough water. Third, I'm referring you to the diabetes education program to meet with a dietitian, and to an eye doctor for a retinal exam. We'll also do kidney function and a urine test today.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: And the blood pressure?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: I'll recheck it at your next visit. If it's still above 130 over 80, we'll start a medication for it. Let's repeat the A1c in three months.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay. That's a lot, but it makes sense.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Check your feet every day, and call us if you notice any sores. See you in three months, Mr. Mitchell.
